policy: The original Platymantis reticulatus Brown et al. 1997 was replaced by P. isarog in 1997; do not confuse it with unrelated historical reticulatus. Comparisons are based on preserved series, not automatic identification.

records.label: Original hazelae-group differential
records.text: The 1997 revision describes a pointed, sometimes knob-tipped snout and a distinct tympanum measuring about 25–42% of eye diameter in its examined series; unlike most other hazelae-group species, it lacks yellow-and-brown areolations in the groin and thighs.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.sourceLocation: Original hazelae Group key, p. 407; P. hazelae Description and Comparisons, pp. 409–410
records.studyScope: Examined Negros/Masbate series, distinct from P. polilloensis by comparative proportions; historic P. rivularis synonymy was treated with reservations. Not a single-character or locality-only identification.

records.label: Observed arboreal fern and Pandanus sites
records.text: The 1997 revision reports P. hazelae chiefly from arboreal ferns and Pandanus leaf axils in submontane and montane Negros forests, with a smaller set of observations from shrubs, stream rocks and lower-elevation dipterocarp forest.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.studyScope: Published Negros and Masbate specimens; documented local microhabitats, not a fixed nationwide elevational cutoff.

records.label: Observed direct-developing eggs
records.text: The revision records clutches of five to nine large unpigmented eggs in arboreal ferns or Pandanus leaf axils, with direct development in observed P. hazelae populations.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.sourceLocation: P. hazelae Reproduction, p. 409, citing Alcala 1962
records.studyScope: Study summary citing earlier original observations; no claim of all-season breeding or universally fixed clutch size.

records.label: Original reticulatus (= isarog) diagnosis
records.text: Described as P. reticulatus Brown et al. (1997), now P. isarog, this Mount Isarog frog has extensive pale brown-bordered areolations onto the lower hind legs, often a brown reticulate ventral pattern, and dark dorsal spots in the examined specimens.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.sourceLocation: P. reticulatus original diagnosis, p. 416, and Comparisons, p. 418; replacement name in Herpetological Review 28:131
records.studyScope: Published 1997 type series, renamed P. isarog after discovery of primary homonymy. Areolations and ventral reticulation vary; no universal field-photo diagnosis. Historical Mount Isarog records are not current site sightings.

records.label: Original Mount Isarog forest microhabitats
records.text: The original Mount Isarog series was collected in submontane and montane forest near 1,100–1,500 m; specimens were observed on birdnest ferns, tree branches and trunks, and the forest floor.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.studyScope: Field records from the 1990s Mount Isarog type series, under the original name P. reticulatus, not an island-wide habitat suitability model.

records.label: Large unpigmented ovarian eggs
records.text: The original description reports large unpigmented eggs in a gravid female P. reticulatus (= P. isarog); the authors recorded no confirmed deposition site or developmental chronology.
records.source: Brown, Brown & Alcala (1997), Proc. California Acad. Sci. 49:405–421
records.studyScope: A single gravid female in the original species description. Egg deposition and development were explicitly unknown.

replacementNameReference.source: Brown, Brown, Alcala & Frost (1997), Herpetological Review 28:131, nomenclatural replacement
replacementNameReference.sourceLocation: Herpetological Review 28(3):131, replacement name isarog for reticulatus Brown et al. 1997
